founded.what: The year two wine merchants from Aachen set up their business at Aÿ, with a third partner, by the trade union's account.

place: Aÿ, Vallée de la Marne, Champagne

kind.means: A négociant manipulant, a house in the trade's own word: it grows part of its fruit, buys more from growers and makes the wine itself, and the Union des Maisons de Champagne lists it among the houses.

story: Deutz began at Aÿ in 1838, when two wine merchants from Aachen, in the German Rhineland, set up in business there with a third partner, under the name Lambry, Geldermann et Deutz, by the account of the Union des Maisons de Champagne. The house carries the name of one of the two, and so does its Pinot Noir led prestige cuvée, Cuvée William Deutz. In 1860 the firm became Deutz et Geldermann, and the two founding families ran it through the nineteenth century. On 5 July 1993 the house of Louis Roederer took sixty per cent of the holding company of Champagne Deutz through an increase of its capital, and in the same year the firm took the single name Deutz, by the union's chronology. The house is made at Aÿ, apart from Roederer's cellars at Reims. Amour de Deutz followed: a Blanc de Blancs launched in 2000 with the 1993 vintage, by the house's own account to greet the new millennium. A Chardonnay prestige cuvée from a Pinot Noir village is the paradox the house likes to point out: its own page calls Amour a cuvée of Chardonnay made on historic Pinot Noir ground. Its making rests on steel vats and blending, and on long ageing in the chalk cellars of Aÿ.

style.line: Fine and elegant rather than powerful: every cru is fermented apart in stainless steel to keep the fruit pure, and blending, not the cellar's vessels, makes the house's signature.
style.grapes: All three grapes of Champagne: Pinot Noir from Aÿ and the Montagne de Reims, Chardonnay from the Côte des Blancs, and Meunier in Brut Classic.
style.reserve: Brut Classic has no fixed formula: the cellar master draws on the house's library of reserve wines from chosen vintages, among them Grand Cru Pinot Noir and Chardonnay, by the house.
style.vessels: Stainless steel vats alone, more than 220 of them for some 90 crus fermented separately, chosen by the house for their neutrality.
style.malolactic: The still wines are first tasted after their alcoholic and malolactic fermentations, which generally end in early to mid January, by the house's bottling letter of 2021.
style.lees: Brut Classic ages three years in the house's cellars, well beyond the appellation's minimum, by the house; the grandes cuvées, Amour among them, 8 to 10 years.

nv.name: Brut Classic
nv.note: The non vintage Brut and the first wine the house makes each year: Chardonnay, Pinot Noir and Meunier with reserve wines, aged three years in the cellars of Aÿ.

cuvee.name: Amour de Deutz

first.what: The first vintage, launched in 2000 to mark the new millennium, by the house's own page.

cuvee.rhythm: Made in vintage years only, since the 1993. The house's and merchants' pages show among others the 2005, 2007, 2008, 2010, 2011, 2013, 2014 and 2015 vintages.
cuvee.blend: Chardonnay alone: a Blanc de Blancs, chiefly from Grand Cru villages of the Côte des Blancs with a touch of Premier Cru.
cuvee.sites: Avize, Le Mesnil-sur-Oger and Oger above all, the Grand Cru villages of the Côte des Blancs. The mix moves by vintage: the 2011 added Villeneuve, Vertus and Villers-Marmery, and the 2015 Chouilly and Vertus.
cuvee.making: Each cru is fermented apart in stainless steel vats, and the malolactic conversion is completed, by the house's importer for the 2015. The blend is bottled the summer after the harvest, the 2015 on 27 June 2016, and rests in the chalk cellars of Aÿ for nine years and more before it is disgorged. The dosage of the 2015 was 6.5 grams a litre, a Brut, by the importer and the Drinks Business.
cuvee.lees: More than nine years, by the house's own page; its bottling letter of 2021 gives 8 to 10 years for the grandes cuvées of the 2020 vintage.
cuvee.young: Lemon and ripe yellow fruit with honey, a dry, chalky line and, on the finish, fresh butter and roasted hazelnut, by the notes of the Drinks Business and Gault et Millau on a single vintage.
cuvee.aged: It comes to the table already mellowed by nine years and more in the cellar. No note read describes a bottle kept long after release, so none is told here.

forms.name: Amour de Deutz Rosé
forms.note: Côte des Blancs Chardonnay blended with red wine from the house's own vineyards of Aÿ, Bouzy and Ambonnay, aged nine years in the chalk cellars.

cuvee.serve: 8 to 10 degrees Celsius, cold but never ice cold; no need to decant; a tulip or a white wine glass.

table.house45: Deutz is a house of Aÿ, founded in 1838 by two wine merchants from Aachen in Germany, and it carries the name of one of them. Aÿ is a Pinot Noir village, yet the house is known for finesse rather than power. Every one of its crus is fermented apart in stainless steel, and the art is in the blending. In 1993 the house of Louis Roederer took a majority, but Deutz is made apart, in Aÿ. Brut Classic, aged three years in the cellar, is its familiar non vintage. Amour de Deutz, a vintage Blanc de Blancs, is the prestige cuvée.
table.house10: Deutz is the elegant house of Aÿ, founded in 1838 by merchants from Aachen, where Louis Roederer took a majority in 1993.
table.cuvee45: Amour de Deutz is a vintage Blanc de Blancs, Chardonnay alone, and the prestige cuvée of the house. Its grapes come mostly from Avize, Le Mesnil and Oger, Grand Cru villages of the Côte des Blancs. Time is its signature: more than nine years in the chalk cellars of Aÿ before it is released. The first vintage was 1993, launched in 2000 for the new millennium. Lemon, honey and roasted hazelnut fill the glass, with a dry, chalky finish. I serve it at about nine degrees in a white wine glass, so it opens as you drink it.
table.sale: Amour de Deutz is pure Côte des Blancs Chardonnay, aged more than nine years before it reaches us. Would you like to try a bottle?
table.cuvee10: Amour de Deutz is the house's vintage Blanc de Blancs, Grand Cru Chardonnay aged more than nine years in the cellar.
table.cuvee20: Amour de Deutz is a vintage Champagne of Chardonnay alone, grown chiefly in the Grand Cru villages of the Côte des Blancs. It rests more than nine years in the chalk cellars of Aÿ, and that time gives it honey and roasted hazelnut.

guests.q: Is Amour de Deutz the house's only prestige cuvée?
guests.a: No. Deutz makes two: Amour de Deutz, the Blanc de Blancs, and Cuvée William Deutz, a Pinot Noir led vintage wine named for the founder. The class sheet names Amour de Deutz.

guests.q: Is Deutz part of Louis Roederer?
guests.a: Louis Roederer took a majority of the house in 1993, but Deutz is made in its own cellars at Aÿ, in its own style.

guests.q: Why make a Blanc de Blancs in a Pinot Noir village?
guests.a: The house is at Aÿ, but the Chardonnay comes from the Côte des Blancs, chiefly Avize, Le Mesnil and Oger. The house itself likes the paradox.

traps: Amour de Deutz is the Blanc de Blancs; Cuvée William Deutz is the Pinot Noir led wine.
Louis Roederer took a majority of Deutz in 1993, but Deutz is not made at Reims: it is made at Aÿ.
Deutz the Champagne house is not Geldermann, the German sparkling wine house of Baden that once shared the old firm name of Deutz et Geldermann.
Hommage à William Deutz is a set of single plot wines of Aÿ, not the prestige cuvée Cuvée William Deutz.

sheet.label: Amour de Deutz
sheet.note: The sheet and the label agree. The sheet names one of the house's two prestige cuvées: Cuvée William Deutz, the Pinot Noir led one, is not on it.

cards.front: Deutz: name the prestige cuvée on the class sheet, and its grape.

cards.back: Deutz, of Aÿ, founded in 1838; Louis Roederer took a majority in 1993.

questions.q: Which prestige cuvée on the class sheet is the vintage Blanc de Blancs of a house founded at Aÿ in 1838?
questions.exp: Amour de Deutz is the Blanc de Blancs of Deutz. Cuvée William Deutz is the house's Pinot Noir led cuvée, Celebris is Gosset's and Comtes de Champagne is Taittinger's Blanc de Blancs, of Reims.

questions.q: In what does Deutz ferment its base wines, by its own account?
opts: Stainless steel vats, each cru apart
New oak barrels from the Argonne
questions.exp: Deutz ferments in stainless steel alone, more than 220 vats for some 90 crus, for the purity of the fruit. Old oak barrels are Bollinger's mark, its neighbour in Aÿ.

questions.q: From which part of Champagne does the Chardonnay of Amour de Deutz chiefly come?
questions.exp: Avize, Le Mesnil-sur-Oger and Oger, Grand Cru villages of the Côte des Blancs, lead the blend. The house stands at Aÿ in the Vallée de la Marne, and the Montagne de Reims gives only a touch in some vintages.

report: Built on the library's p-deutz and contradicting none of it: founded 1838, Aÿ, Roederer's majority from 1993, made apart, Amour the Blanc de Blancs and William Deutz the Pinot Noir led cuvée.
The 1993 stake is dated 5 July 1993 and sixty per cent by the Union des Maisons de Champagne; Wikipedia dates the Rouzaud family's purchase to 1983, which the record does not follow.

The founders' dates differ between accounts (the second founder 1811 to 1872 in one, 1810 to 1869 in another), so the founders are described, and William Deutz is named only as the house's and the cuvée's name.

Left out for want of a second source: the warehouses of the firm burned in the riots of April 1911 (contemporary press reports only), and the year the German branch was split off (1988, Wikipedia alone).
The first vintage of Cuvée William Deutz was not found, so the record gives it none; the planner's 1959 is not taught.
style.dosage is empty: no house page read gives Brut Classic's dosage. Amour's 6.5 grams a litre for the 2015 rests on the importer and the Drinks Business.
The malolactic line is the house's bottling letter for the range, and Amour's completed malolactic is the importer's for the 2015.
The house's brochure lists Brut Classic as predominantly Chardonnay, Pinot Noir and Meunier without saying which leads, so the record names the three and no share.
kind.code: the letters NM were not read on a label; the Union des Maisons de Champagne lists Maison Deutz among the houses. A refuter should read a label.
cuvee.aged tells no long aged glass: no note read describes one. cuvee.bottle is empty: no story of the bottle was sourced.
say is the German saying of the name; no source for how the house or the French say it was read. style.dosage is empty because the house does not state it on any page read.
Refuter: say is now the French saying, DUHTS, the vowel of deux; the German DOYTS was the author's, and the house is French.

changed: story, table.house45: William Deutz is no longer named as a person, since his dates were not found; the house and the cuvée Cuvée William Deutz carry the name as labels.
table.house10: Louis Roederer as majority owner since 1993 told as a present state; now dated history, the majority taken in 1993 (the Union des Maisons de Champagne, the Decanter profile).
traps[1]: the library's present tense majority owned now reads as dated history, the majority taken in 1993.

traps[2]: the German sparkling wine is Geldermann, of Baden, not a wine named Deutz: the firm was split into Champagne Deutz and the Badische Geldermann sparkling wine house (wein.plus, Wikipedia); the split stays undated.
say and cuvee.say: DOYTS, the German saying, became DUHTS, the French vowel of deux, as French speakers and one pronunciation guide say it.
open: The French saying rests on one guide's dirts and the French reading of eu; a recording from the house was not heard.
NM was not read on a label; the Union des Maisons de Champagne lists Deutz among its houses.
Brut Classic's blend: one merchant gives equal thirds, another 45, 30 and 25 with Chardonnay leading, so the record still names the three grapes and no share.
